StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

BeforeSideTurnStart.issue: FIXED, not just re-recorded. Replaced `combat._rng.sample(...) (shared unseeded rng, reservoir algorithm) with `combat.combat_rng.card_selection` + an in-place `.shuffle()` + slice — the named `CombatCardSelection` stream in parity mode, algorithmically matching `UnstableShuffle(...).Take(...)`. The record's reasoning was correct; only the verdict needed to move from open gap to fixed. Pinned by `test/test_r14_powers.py::TestAggression` (3 tests).

guards.rationale: powers.py:505-506 `player is not self.owner -> return`. The enemy side cannot hold Aggression (its body reaches Owner.Player), so the per-creature-vs-per-side problem does not arise for this unit.

guards.what: AggressionPower.cs:27 `c.Type == CardType.Attack` over the DISCARD pile
guards.rationale: powers.py:511 filters player.discard_pile on CardType.ATTACK. Identical pile and identical predicate.

guards.what: AggressionPower.cs:28 `.Take(base.Amount)` with fewer candidates than Amount
guards.rationale: LINQ Take silently yields what exists; powers.py:514's `min(self.amount, len(candidates))` does the same, and powers.py:512-513 returns early on an empty pile. No off-by-one.

powers.py:518-519 tests `card.upgrade_level == 0`. Equivalent for the ported pool -- every sim card is single-upgrade -- and the comment says so. A multi-level upgradable card would expose the difference; none exists.

guards.what: AggressionPower.cs:31 CardPileCmd.Add(card, PileType.Hand) before the upgrade
guards.rationale: powers.py:516-519 moves the card then upgrades, in the same order. The sim mutates the piles directly rather than through CardPileCmd, so no on_card_drawn / MaxCardsInHand handling fires -- the pile-verb question belongs to creature_card_cmds, not to this unit.
